title: Cybersecurity Labeling for Internet of Things
summary: In this document, the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau (Bureau) of the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) seeks comment on recommendations for the U.S. Cyber Trust Mark (USCTM) program, a voluntary cybersecurity labeling program for wireless consumer Internet of Things (IoT) products. The Bureau seeks comment on the design and placement of the FCC IoT Label, display of product registry information, certification renewal, post-market surveillance, and procedures for complaints, noncompliant products, and program administrators that withdraw or whose authority is terminated. These actions would support the establishment and effective administration of the USCTM program and provide consumers with accessible cybersecurity information about certified IoT products.

title: Employee or Independent Contractor Status Under the Fair Labor Standards Act, Family and Medical Leave Act, and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act
summary: This final rule rescinds the analysis for determining employee or independent contractor status under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA or Act) set forth in the Department of Labor's (Department) regulations and replaces it with an analysis similar to what it published in a final rule promulgated in 2021, with several modifications and enhancements. In addition, this final rule amends provisions in the Department's regulations implementing the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA) to provide that employee or independent contractor status under those laws should be determined using the Department's FLSA analysis, as the FMLA and MSPA both incorporate the FLSA's scope of employment.

title: Marine Mammals; Incidental Take During Specified Activities; Proposed Incidental Harassment Authorization for Southwest Alaska Stock of Northern Sea Otters in Kodiak, Alaska
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS or we), in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972, as amended, from the City of Kodiak, propose to authorize incidental take by harassment of small numbers of Southwest Alaska stock northern sea otters (Enhydra lutris kenyoni) from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2027. The applicant has requested this authorization for take by harassment that may result from activities associated with pile driving and marine construction within St. Herman Harbor in Kodiak, Alaska. We estimate that this project may result in the incidental take by harassment of up to 324 northern sea otters from the Southwest Alaska stock. Neither the applicant nor the FWS anticipated any lethal take. We invite comments on the proposed incidental harassment authorization and the accompanying draft environmental assessment from the public, Tribes, and local, State, and Federal agencies.

summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972, as amended, from the Alaska Railroad Corporation, propose to authorize incidental take by harassment of small numbers of Southcentral Alaska stock northern sea otters (Enhydra lutris kenyoni) for a period of up to 1 year. title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.
